newsitem.title: UK: Northern uses London bid in defence.
newsitem.headline: Northern uses London bid in defence.

text.p: Bid target Northern Electric said on Wednesday that it should be worth 780 pence a share using a comparison with an agreed bid for fellow regional electricity company (Rec) London from Entergy of the U.S.
In a statement, it said the offer for London at 705 pence per share "re-emphasises the cheapness of CE Electric's bid for Northern Electric."
CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy of the U.S., is offering 670 pence per share for Northern in a hostile bid which closes on December 20.
It has already bought nearly 30 percent of Northern on the market at its original bid price of 630 pence per share.
Northern has consistently argued that CE Electric's bid undervalues the company and used various comparisons to indicate a stronger valuation.
CE Electric said that the bid for London should reassure investors that future bids for other Recs would not be adversely affected by the price offered for Northern.
"Institutional concerns about lower bids are overdone," a spokesman said.
Institutions had expressed worries that acceptance of CE Electric's bid would have a knock-on effect on levels for the three remaining Recs, which included London.
